en: Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.47. The Triplet on the Visible and the Dyad on the Rooted The Triplet on the Visible and the Dyad on the Rooted:
Exposition of the Positive and Negative Methods of the Triplets and Dyads. 16.47. Sanidassanattika, Sahetukaduka.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with-root, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and without-root,
by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with-root, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor with-reactive and without-root,
by way of root-condition …pe… dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and with-root … [and so forth].
Dependent on states that are non-non-indicative-and-reactive and non-non-causal, there arise states that are non-non-indicative-and-reactive and non-non-causal by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are six; under object-condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are six.

Dependent on a state that is non-indicative, non-reactive, and non-causal, there arises a state that is non-non-indicative-and-reactive and non-non-causal by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are three.
